items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Jimmy Condon just died, and that's the guy that he played with most of the year.

ctx.x: Yes, he did, but I don't know what ever happened to him. Nobody else knows. You ask everybody what happened to Dink, and nobody can tell you. Dink wasn't his name. That was a nickname. And I asked for his name, and I couldn't tell you to save my life.
I think I found it somewhere. I know Herbert Hall has gone on with Eddie Condon.

Yeah, he's getting ready to settle in Texas. He's going to come south again? That's right. They bought his wife. We introduced his wife to him when we first came to San Antonio, Texas. And he married her right around 20, around 29 or 30. And her parents are from a little town of Bernie, and they had a lot of land up there. And they willed it to his wife. Mm-hmm. So Herbert visited me sometime this year. Mm-hmm. And they built a fabulous home up there, and he's leaving New York altogether. Well, I can understand…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: Yeah, well you've got Pops Foster and Paul Ballgren, Monty Johnson and Eddie Conda and Louie Russell.

ctx.x: Yeah, well you've got Pops Foster and Paul Ballgren, Monty Johnson and Eddie Conda and Louie Russell.
Oh, they're just playing. That's all you know. Yeah. That's another one of these great big tones that we call a balloon tone.
